messages:
marco: Hey folks, first-week headache: I cloned the repo, ran `docker compose up` and the app can't reach Postgres (app logs: `psycopg2.OperationalError: could not connect to server: Connection refused\nIs the server running on host \"db\" (172.19.0.2) and accepting TCP/IP connections on port 5432?`). I don't have a local Postgres running, so not sure why it's refusing. Any quick checks?

lia: Hi Marco — welcome! A few things to check: 1) Are you on macOS with Colima/Docker Desktop? 2) Do you have any host-level Postgres occupying 5432? Run `lsof -i :5432` to see. If host Postgres is running, compose's port mapping might be failing to bind and the container DB might not start.

marco: I'm on mac + Colima. lsof shows nothing on 5432. `docker ps` shows our db container is up. `docker logs repo_db_1` shows `FATAL: could not create lock file` and then shuts down.

sean: That FATAL usually means the container can't write to the volume mount. Check your data volume path permissions. If you're using a host path (./data/db:/var/lib/postgresql/data) on mac+colima, the FS driver sometimes needs `chown` or a named volume. Try switching to a named volume in compose: `db_data:` under `volumes:` and `- db_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` in the service.

lia: Another common issue: if you previously started the container as root, the mounted folder on host may be root-owned. `docker-compose down && sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ./data/db` (or rm the directory if you don't need the data) then `docker compose up`.

marco: Switched to a named volume and recreated, db stays up now but app still can't connect. App env has `DATABASE_HOST=db` and `DATABASE_PORT=5432`. When I `docker exec -it repo_app_1 ping db` it resolves. But the app still errors with timeout.

sean: If the app is in a separate compose project or using host networking, it might not be on the same Docker network. Ensure both services are in same compose file or share a network. Also confirm the app container's env isn't accidentally using `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`. Inside the app container, run `psql -h db -U postgres -p 5432 -c '\l'` to test. If that works, the issue is app config, not Postgres.

marco: `psql` inside app container failed with "could not connect to server: Connection timed out". Strange.

lia: Timeout suggests networking or firewall between containers. On mac with Colima, there are occasional DNS/bridge issues. Try `docker network inspect repo_default` and confirm both container IDs are listed. If they are and ping works, check the Postgres `listen_addresses` in the container (`postgresql.conf`) — our image should default to `*`, but some custom images limit it. Also verify `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD` is not blocking.

devex-bot: Quick checklist: 1) Volume perms 2) Service on same network 3) Postgres listening on 0.0.0.0 4) No port collision on host 5) Try `docker compose logs -f db` for startup errors. Docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/local-postgres

sean: Another thing: if your app uses host-side tooling (like running the app on host rather than inside container), `db` won't resolve from host. Use `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` and map port in compose: `ports: - \"5433:5432\"` and set `DATABASE_PORT=5433` locally to avoid colliding with host Postgres.

marco: Ah — I was running the app locally (not in container) during debug. I changed env to `DATABASE_HOST=127.0.0.1` and mapped `5433:5432` in compose, started db, and now app connects. Thanks! One follow-up: we have a migration init script that installs `pgvector`. It failed inside container with `ERROR: could not open extension control file`. Any tips for installing extensions in dev compose?

lia: For pgvector you need the extension available in the Postgres image. We maintain a Dockerfile `docker/postgres/Dockerfile` that installs `postgresql-contrib` or builds/installs pgvector from source for the right Postgres version. Add `image: local-postgres:14` in compose and build with `docker compose build db`. Alternatively, run the `psql` command after container is up to create extension using a shared init script under `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` (only works on first init).

ops-bot: Reminder: do not commit compiled extension binaries or host-specific data to the repo. Use named volumes and documented rebuild steps in `infra/README.md`.

marco: Perfect — switching to named volume + mapped port fixed connectivity. I'll follow up on the pgvector Dockerfile. Thanks everyone and hi all! :)

lia: Welcome again! Tag @devex if you want a quick pairing session to walk through the compose files.
